findings.title: VoteMarket ETH affordability can stop pending settlement
Constructors accept the new contract itself as owner
Votium's cap and exclusion terms are live for future deposits even on an older listing. They affect venue allocation inputs, not the custody recipient; monitor authorized updates.
Confiscation is based on the current authoritative kill flag, not a minimum kill duration. A committed confiscation is terminal if the flag later clears. Keep this policy explicit.
The first maturity is the next aligned week boundary, not a full week after payment. Display the scheduled boundary rather than a minimum one-week lock.
`handlerId` selects a pool-local slot among matching MetaRegistry handlers, not a global handler identifier. Clarify this in the interface documentation.
The default build source set includes test mocks and the fixture-only ERC-20 interface. Select the production artifact identities explicitly.

Standalone FeeDistributor maintenance success does not attest full allocation coverage. A positive pre-existing delta outside the distributor's bounded coverage can be incompletely allocated; the guarded confiscation path is separate.
VoteMarket's private receipt field stays zero for layout stability; the public getters derive the receipt. Use the getters and events rather than raw storage for evidence.
`SafeToken` masks dependency revert bytes, and a malformed Boolean can fail at the decoder rather than the named error. Keep monitoring compatible with both failure forms.
Unsolicited crvUSD does not create listing credit or a sweep right. Adapters preserve their pre-deposit balances.
The mock remote manager checks exact configured ETH value; the production manager forwards supplied value to the messenger. Fixture success is not bridge pricing or refund evidence.
The mock controller grants a designated lister its own addition route; the raw reference controller has an incumbent-admin gate. Do not infer production authority from the mock.
The adapters retain string reverts for ownership proposal and acceptance while the core uses custom errors. Preserve that distinction in diagnostic decoders.
Zero-first approval and final allowance clearing add explicit token calls. Retain those checks unless a replacement is shown to preserve custody and failure behavior.
A zero `confiscate` return can mean an Active, un-killed listing or a terminal record. Use record status and the completion event to distinguish outcomes.
